archetype.name: Point Guard (screen-heavy)
archetype.definition: A distributor in Sean Payton's offense who lives on screens and quick throws, almost never takes a sack, and takes occasional deep shots rather than working the intermediate middle.

report.headline: Low-volume, sack-proof distributor whose passing has finally caught up to the wins
report.take:
Bo Nix in his third season is a quarterback whose value sits in what he avoids more than in what he piles up. His sack rate of 3.6% ranks 3rd of 55. His offense allows hits on just 9.2% of dropbacks, 2nd in the league. Only 17.5% of his pressures become sacks, which matches the 17.2% rate he posted in 2025. That is a stable, career-long trait, not a hot streak. The rest of the profile is modest: 6.07 yards per attempt (40th), a 59.9% completion rate (39th) and 195.5 passing yards a game. Still, his 0.023 EPA per dropback sits comfortably above the league's -0.027, because he rarely gives away a down.

The passing EPA comes almost entirely from two depths. Throws of 0-9 air yards produce 0.165 EPA per attempt with a +3.8 CPOE and 8 of his 12 TDs. His 34 deep shots return 0.221 EPA even though only 32.4% are completed. Pulling the other way are 83 attempts behind the line of scrimmage, which have cost 14.2 EPA. The intermediate game is also broken: 42.9% completions, a -9.7 CPOE and 3 of his 5 interceptions. Throws over the middle carry a -17.4 CPOE on 36 attempts. The offense looks better under center (0.183 EPA) than in shotgun (-0.015), and it plays well late in close games (0.201 EPA in fourth-quarter one-score situations).

The topline numbers hide two things. First, the drop in completion rate from 2025 (-3.5 points) is not a raw-accuracy problem. His charted bad-throw rate actually fell from 15.2% to 12.7%. The decline comes from where the ball goes and who catches it: Courtland Sutton is at -0.147 EPA on 49 targets, while Pat Bryant's 0.771 on 22 targets is a small-sample spike that will cool. Second, the rushing has collapsed. Designed runs average 1.57 yards, a third are stuffed and none have broken big. His rushing yards per game are down 8.8 from last year, and in the last three games he has run for almost nothing. That removes a piece of his fantasy floor that two prior seasons of 350-430 rushing yards had made dependable.

The direction is good. Over his last three games his EPA per dropback is 0.143, up 0.12 on his season mark, and his CPOE has climbed to +0.4. Denver has won all five games since Week 6. The early KC loss (-11.5 EPA) and the Seattle and Chargers slogs are dragging the season line. The version of Nix playing now is a solid, efficient game-runner, even if the yardage will stay ordinary in an offense built around short throws.

strengths.title: Sacks almost never happen
strengths.body: He avoids sacks better than almost anyone, and his line keeps him clean: Denver's offensive hit rate ranks 2nd. His pressure-to-sack rate has been top-10 in each of his three seasons. That makes it a durable trait that keeps drives on schedule, not a lucky run.

strengths.title: Short game is efficient and accurate
strengths.body: Throws of 0-9 air yards are the engine: a +3.8 CPOE, 0.165 EPA per attempt and most of his touchdowns. This is the core of the Payton system and it should hold, though it caps his yardage ceiling.

strengths.title: Recent passing surge
strengths.body: His last three games have been his best stretch: the CPOE turned positive and per-game passing EPA rose sharply. The opponents were mixed (KC's 5th-ranked defense, plus Carolina and Las Vegas), so the gains aren't purely schedule-driven.

concerns.title: Third downs are a sinkhole
concerns.body: On third down his EPA per play is -0.248, and Denver converts just 28.9% at an average of 7.6 yards to go. Long-yardage situations demand the intermediate throws he isn't hitting, so this is a real limitation, not bad luck. It will persist unless early downs get shorter.

concerns.title: Intermediate and middle throws misfire
concerns.body: Throws of 10-19 air yards and anything over the middle come in well below expected completion, and they account for most of his interceptions. His bad-throw rate has improved, so the cause looks more like receivers and decisions on those routes than raw accuracy. Sutton's negative per-target EPA fits that picture.

concerns.title: Rushing floor has vanished
concerns.body: Designed runs have been stuffed constantly and average under two yards. His rushing output is well below last season's. Outside one 73-yard game in Arizona he has added little on the ground, which thins his fantasy floor.

trend.note: After negative-EPA games in Weeks 1, 5 and 6, he has posted positive passing EPA in four straight games, with Weeks 8-9 his best of the year. Denver has won five straight since Week 6.

nextGame.headline: Low total, possible wind, and a defense stingy on short throws
nextGame.body:
Pittsburgh's defense is built to squeeze exactly what Nix does best. It ranks 8th against short passes and 4th against the run, and it has allowed the 5th-fewest fantasy points to quarterbacks. Two openings exist. The Steelers are 25th against deep passes and 24th in explosive passes allowed, which fits his productive deep shots. They have also been one of the league's worst units against tight ends, which points to Evan Engram (0.125 EPA per target). Their 38.5 total is lower than any game Denver has played this year, so the volume ceiling is limited.

Availability tilts toward Denver's protection. Pittsburgh is without Nick Herbig and likely without Alex Highsmith, two edge rushers who play a combined majority of snaps, against a defense with a 6th-ranked sack rate. That should make Nix's sack avoidance even harder to crack. On the other side, Pittsburgh expects Michael Pittman Jr. back but has lost guard Mason McCormick, which could slow its top-ranked rushing attack and keep the game low-scoring. The forecast is early, but it shows 17 mph wind with gusts near 39 and drizzle. If that holds, it would mute the deep game he needs against this secondary and push him further into the short throws Pittsburgh defends well.

keyMatchups.title: Deep shots vs leaky deep coverage
keyMatchups.body: His deep attempts return strong EPA despite a low completion rate, and Pittsburgh bleeds EPA on deep passes. It is his best path to a big game. Wind is the threat that could take it away.

keyMatchups.title: Engram against a soft TE defense
keyMatchups.body: Pittsburgh ranks 30th in EPA allowed to lead tight ends. Engram has been one of his more efficient targets. With the WR1 role facing the league's 3rd-stingiest coverage, the tight end is the logical pressure point.

keyMatchups.title: Depleted edge rush
keyMatchups.body: Pittsburgh's sack rate ranks 6th, but losing Herbig and likely Highsmith blunts it. That plays into the clean-pocket offense Nix already runs.

nextGame.watch: Whether the wind lets Denver take its deep shots or forces him into Pittsburgh's strength underneath.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect the recent version more than the season line. The sack avoidance, the short-game efficiency and the winning game scripts are sustainable. They held across his first two seasons and have strengthened lately. Two things will likely cool. Pat Bryant's per-target efficiency is a small-sample outlier, and deep EPA built on a third of attempts being completed swings week to week. The yardage ceiling stays modest in a screen-heavy, pass-funnel-light scheme. Something like 195-235 passing yards and 1.0-1.6 TDs a game is the realistic band, with 13-18 fantasy points.

The swing is the ground game and third downs. If designed runs start working again, as they did for two seasons, his floor rises by a few points a week. If the intermediate game stays broken, Denver will keep stalling on third-and-long and settling for field goals, which caps his TD rate.
swingFactors: Late-season weather hitting the deep game

confidence.note: Ten starts with a clear recent upswing, but key splits rest on small samples.
